data.name: FileSharingCard.Description
data.value: On by default: the folders chosen below show in Android's shared storage, in the Host folder, so Android apps can open and save files there. Android apps reach them only with Android's storage permission, and Windows lets them do only what your own account may do.

data.name: SharedFoldersCard.Description

data.name: AndroidFilesCard.Description
data.value: Opens Android's shared storage in File Explorer: the files Android apps saved, such as photos and downloads. Android starts if it is not running. Android in File Explorer's navigation pane does the same.

data.name: FilesNote.Text
data.value: To send a file to an Android app, drag it from File Explorer onto the app's window. An APK you drop is installed.

data.name: LinksCard.Header
data.value: Open web links in Android apps

data.name: LinksCard.Description
data.value: Off by default: a web link you tap in an Android app opens in your default browser in Windows. On, it opens in an Android app, as on a phone. A link an installed app has verified as its own opens in that app either way.

data.name: ArmCard.Header
data.value: Run apps built only for ARM

data.name: ArmCard.Description
data.value: Many Android apps contain code only for ARM processors. They install and run here only through an ARM translator. Android uses the open source translator that comes with it, unless you install another ARM translation package (dsa arm-translation install) or Google's translator. This switch decides whether Android uses a translator at all; it applies from the next start of Android. Only 64-bit ARM apps (arm64-v8a) can run.

data.name: ArmRestartBar.Message
data.value: Android started before this change. Stop and start Android for ARM apps to follow it.

data.name: Arm_DefaultDescription
data.value: {0} {1} ({2}) comes with this Android and is used unless you install another translator. Going back to it removes the package installed in its place, from the next start of Android.

data.name: Arm_SupportedDefault
data.value: Supported by {0} {1} ({2}), the translator that comes with this Android.

data.name: ArmRemoveCard.Description
data.value: Deletes the package from your add-on disk. ARM apps you installed stay, but do not run after Android restarts.

data.name: Arm_NotSupported
data.value: Not supported: no ARM translation package is installed.

data.name: Arm_TurnedOff

data.name: Arm_NotRunning
data.value: Android is not running, so what it supports now is not known.

data.name: ArmGoogleCard.Description
data.value: Gets the ARM translator from the Android emulator image Google offers for this Android version and installs it as a translation package. DSA does not include or pass on Google's translator: your computer downloads the image from Google, under Google's Android SDK License, keeps only the translator and deletes the rest (about 2 GB). Nothing is downloaded until you agree. A package built from another translator, such as Digitalis, does the same job.

data.name: ArmGoogle_Notice
data.value: DSA downloads the Android emulator image for this Android version from Google's SDK repository ({0}) and takes out only its ARM translator. The translator is Google's software, offered under the Android SDK License ({1}); by downloading it you accept those terms. DSA does not ship or pass it on. The image is about 2 GB and is deleted afterwards. The translator works from the next start of Android.

data.name: ArmGoogleFetchingBar.Message
data.value: Downloading about 2 GB from Google and taking the translator out. This takes a few minutes.

data.name: GappsCard.Header
data.value: Google Play services and Play Store

data.name: GappsCard.Description
data.value: DSA does not include Google's apps. When you ask, it downloads LiteGapps Core, a public package of Google Play services, the Play Store and the account sync components made for this Android version, and installs it. It applies from the next start of Android.

data.value: Downloading and installing Google Play. This can take several minutes.

data.name: GappsTermsCard.Description
data.value: Google Play services and the Play Store are Google's software and follow Google's terms. DSA does not distribute them: it downloads the public LiteGapps package only when you ask for it.

data.name: GappsRegisterCard.Description

data.name: AppsDpiScaling.ToolTip
data.value: Who scales this app when its window moves to a monitor of another scale. System: the app keeps its scale and DSA scales its window to the same physical size; text can look a little blurry. Automatic picks App for apps that say they handle it, and System for the others. Automatic and System never restart the app.

data.name: AdvancedNetworkingCard.Description
data.value: Off by default. When on, Android joins this PC's network as a device of its own: other devices on the network can reach Android apps, and Android apps can reach them directly. Programs on this PC can always reach a server in Android at the address above.

data.name: NetworkRestartBar.Message
data.value: The change applies the next time Android starts. Stop Android on the General page, then open an app.

data.name: HostCertificatesCard.Header
data.value: Use this PC's added root certificates

data.name: HostCertificatesCard.Description
data.value: On by default. Android apps trust the root certificates that you or an administrator added to this PC, such as your company's or a security program's, so sites that need them open in Android too. The root certificates that come with Windows are not listed. The change applies at once.

data.name: CertificatesNone.Text
data.value: No added root certificates were found on this PC.

data.name: Certificate_SourceMachineGroupPolicy
data.value: This PC's Trusted Root Certification Authorities, set by Group Policy

data.name: Certificate_SourceMachineEnterprise
data.value: This PC's Trusted Root Certification Authorities, set by your organization

data.name: Certificate_SourceUserGroupPolicy
data.value: Your Trusted Root Certification Authorities, set by Group Policy

data.name: Certificate_SourceAdmin
data.value: Added by an administrator of this PC

data.name: Certificate_SourceSystem
data.value: Added to the system's certificate store

data.name: BackupCard.Description
data.value: Android backs up its apps' data to a folder in your user folder, encrypted with a key Windows keeps for you. Restore it after a data reset, or on another PC with the recovery key.

data.name: BackupRestoreConfirm.Title
data.value: Restore apps' data from the backup?

data.name: RecoveryKeyCard.Description
data.value: The recovery key opens your backup on another PC, or after Windows was reinstalled. Without it, only this Windows account on this PC can read the backup.

data.name: UseRecoveryKeyCard.Description
data.value: To restore a backup made on another PC, copy its DSA Backup folder into your user folder and enter the recovery key it was made with.

data.name: Backup_NoService
data.value: The DSA service did not say where your backup stands. Open this page again in a moment.

data.name: Backup_Unavailable
data.value: The backup folder or its key cannot be used now.

data.name: Backup_Done
data.value: Backed up the data of {0} apps.

data.name: Backup_DoneSome
data.value: Backed up the data of {0} apps; {1} could not be backed up.

data.name: Backup_Restored
data.value: Restored the data of {0} apps and installed {1} apps.

data.name: Backup_RestoredSome
data.value: Restored the data of {0} apps and installed {1} apps; {2} could not be restored.

data.name: Backup_RestoreWarning
data.value: Each app in the backup gets its data from the backup, in place of what it has now. Apps that are missing are installed again. Android starts if it is not running.

data.name: Backup_KeyAdvice
data.value: Write the key down or keep it in a password manager, away from this PC. Anyone with the key and your backup folder can read the backup.

data.name: Backup_KeyUsed
data.value: The recovery key is kept as your backup key. The backup folder made with it can now be restored here.

data.name: BackupSwitchCard.Header
data.value: Back up apps' data to this PC

data.name: BackupSwitchCard.Description
data.value: Keeps a second copy of your Android apps' user data on this PC, encrypted, so it can be restored after a data reset or on another PC. It is off until you turn it on.

data.name: Backup_Off
data.value: Backup is off. No backup is made, and nothing of the apps' data is kept on this PC.

data.name: Backup_OffKept
data.value: Backup is off. Earlier backups of {0} apps ({1}) are still kept in your DSA Backup folder.

data.name: Backup_DeleteQuestion
data.value: The backups of {0} apps ({1}) are still kept on this PC. Delete them and their key as well, or keep them for a later restore?

data.name: Backup_TurnedOn
data.value: Backup is on. Android backs up its apps' data to this PC from now on.

data.name: Backup_TurnedOff
data.value: Backup is off. The backups made so far are kept.

data.name: Backup_TurnedOffDeleted
data.value: Backup is off, and the backups and their key were deleted.

data.name: KeyProtection_None
data.value: Android's keys get their protection the first time Android starts.

data.name: KeyProtection_Tpm
data.value: Sealed by this PC's TPM. A copy of Android's disk cannot open the apps' keys or Android's encrypted storage anywhere else.

data.name: KeyProtection_Dpapi
data.value: Kept by Windows for your account only, because this PC has no TPM that can be used. A copy of Android's disk still cannot open the keys without your account. Once a TPM works, DSA seals the keys with it.

data.name: KeyProblemBar.Title
data.value: Android's keys could not be opened

data.name: ResetDataCard.Description
data.value: Erases every app you installed, your accounts and the data of every app, so Android starts as it was first installed. The Android image and these settings stay.

data.name: ResetData_Warning
data.value: This erases every app you installed in Android, the accounts you signed in to and the data of every app. Android stops now, and its next start is as it was first installed. The Android image and DSA's settings stay. This cannot be undone.

data.name: ResetDoneBar.Message
data.value: The next app you open starts Android as it was first installed.

data.name: Android_Switching
data.value: Android {0} is chosen. It is downloaded now and used the next time Android starts.

data.name: AndroidChooseCard.Description
data.value: DSA supports the latest two Android versions. Some apps run on only one of them.

data.name: AndroidChooseNote.Text
data.value: Every user of this computer runs the same Android version, so changing it needs an administrator. Security updates for the chosen version keep coming. When a version stops being supported, DSA moves to the next one and keeps your apps.

data.name: AndroidUpConfirm.Body
data.value: Android {0} is downloaded and used the next time Android starts. Your apps and their data move along. Moving back later erases the data.

data.name: AndroidDownConfirm.Title
data.value: Erase Android data to move to an older version?

data.name: Android_DownWarning
data.value: Android {0} is older than the Android {1} that runs now, and Android cannot read data a newer version wrote. Moving erases the Android data of every user of this computer: every app they installed, the accounts they signed in to and the data of every app. Each user's Android then starts as it was first installed. DSA's settings stay. This cannot be undone.

data.name: ApkWindow_AbiWarningTitle
data.value: This app may not run on this PC

data.name: Apps_RunAsArm_system-app
data.value: Apps that are part of Android run as Android installed them.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArm_no-arm-libraries
data.value: No APK of this app on the device holds its ARM code.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArm_translation-off
data.value: ARM translation is not on. Turn it on under ARM apps and restart Android.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArm_arm-only
data.value: This app has only ARM code, so it always runs as ARM.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArm_unknown
data.value: This version of DSA cannot say whether the app can run as ARM.

data.name: AppsRunAsArmEraseBody
data.value: Android cannot change how {0} runs and keep its data. Installing it again erases its data: sign-ins, settings and files it keeps for itself.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArmKept
data.value: {0} was left as it was, with its data.

data.name: Apps_RunAsArmRefused_no-libraries
data.value: its APKs on the device hold no code for that

data.name: ApkWindow_BundleSummary
data.value: {0} comes as several APKs. The {1} this PC needs are installed together, {2} in all.

data.name: ApkWindow_BundleSummaryObb
data.value: {0} comes as several APKs. The {1} this PC needs are installed together with its expansion files, {2} in all.

data.name: Install_Reason_app-bundle
data.value: it is an Android App Bundle, made to be uploaded to an app store. Get the app as an APK, or as an .xapk, .apks or .apkm bundle.

data.name: Install_Reason_encrypted-bundle
data.value: the bundle is encrypted, so its APKs cannot be read. Get the app as an APK, or as a newer bundle.

data.name: Install_Reason_split-signature-mismatch
data.value: a split APK of the bundle is signed with another key than its base APK, so Android would refuse it.

data.name: Install_Reason_invalid-bundle
data.value: the bundle is not one app that Android can install.

data.name: ApkWindow_Reason_app-bundle
data.value: It is an Android App Bundle, made to be uploaded to an app store. Get the app as an APK, or as an .xapk, .apks or .apkm bundle.

data.name: ApkWindow_Reason_encrypted-bundle
data.value: The bundle is encrypted, so its APKs cannot be read. Get the app as an APK, or as a newer bundle.

data.name: ApkWindow_Reason_split-signature-mismatch
data.value: A split APK of the bundle is signed with another key than its base APK, so Android would refuse it.

data.name: ApkWindow_Reason_invalid-bundle
data.value: The bundle is not one app that Android can install.

data.name: ApkWindow_Reason_translation-off
data.value: The app runs only as ARM code (arm64-v8a), and ARM translation is not on. Turn it on under ARM apps, restart Android, and install the app again.

data.name: Android_UpToDate
data.value: No Android update is waiting. DSA checks every day, and restarts Android into an update once no app window is open.

data.name: Android_RestartPending
data.value: Android {0} is downloaded. Restart Android to use it now.

data.name: AndroidRestartConfirm.Body
data.value: Android restarts into Android {0}. Its app windows close; open the apps again once it has started.

data.name: ImageAutoRestartCard.Header
data.value: Restart Android into updates by itself

data.name: ImageAutoRestartCard.Description
data.value: On by default. With no app window open, Android restarts into a downloaded update at once. With windows open, DSA asks first, or waits until you close them. Off, an update is used the next time you start Android.

data.name: Apps_RootTip_unavailable
data.value: Root access is off for this PC. An administrator turns it on in Advanced.

data.name: Apps_RootTip_unknown
data.value: The DSA service does not report this app's root level. Update DSA to choose it here.

data.name: Apps_RootNotChanged
data.value: The root level of {0} was not changed: {1}

data.name: Apps_RootSet_off
data.value: {0} cannot use root any more. su disappears for it from the next start of Android.

data.name: Apps_RootSet_ask
data.value: {0} now asks an administrator of this PC each time it uses su. If it could not see su before, it sees it from the next start of Android.

data.name: Apps_RootSet_remember
data.value: {0} now uses su without asking. If it could not see su before, it sees it from the next start of Android.

data.name: AppsRootOffBar.Message
data.value: No app can use su. An administrator of this PC can turn root access on in Advanced, and then you choose each app's level here.

data.name: AppsRootNote.Text
data.value: Root access: Not allowed hides su from the app. Ask each time shows an administrator prompt with the app's name for each request, and after an approval the app is not asked again for 15 minutes. Remember approves without asking, so choosing it needs an administrator's approval.

data.name: RootElevationCard.Header
data.value: Let Android apps ask for root

data.name: RootElevationCard.Description
data.value: An app you allow on the Apps page can run commands as root once an administrator of this PC approves, as sudo does. Off by default. The Android image, its build properties and SELinux stay as they are.

data.name: RootElevationAdminReason.Text
data.value: Only an administrator can change this, because it applies to every user of this PC. Use Change as administrator, and Windows asks for permission.

data.name: RootElevationRestartBar.Message
data.value: Root access changes from the next start of Android. Stop Android on the General page, then open an app.

data.name: RootElevation_LogAt
data.value: Each request is kept in the service log with the app, the time, whether it was approved and the command: {0}

data.name: RootElevation_LogUnknown
data.value: Each request is kept in the service log with the app, the time, whether it was approved and the command.

data.name: RootNote.Text
data.value: Choose each app's level on the Apps page. Each user chooses for the apps in their own Android.
